shortDescription: Nordic forward power prices fell on Friday weighed down by lower European gas and German power markets, while forecasts pointing to wetter weather in the hydropower-dependent region also weighed.

children: Nordic forward power prices fell on Friday weighed down by lower European gas and German power markets, while forecasts pointing to wetter weather in the hydropower-dependent region also weighed.
Nordic front-quarter baseload power contract (NSBLQc1) fell 1.3 euros or 1.16% to 110.7 euros per megawatt hour (MWh)at 1055 GMT. The contract was down about 2% for the week so far.
Nordic front-year (NSBLYc1) lost 0.35 euros or 0.51% to 67.9 euros per megawatt hour (MWh).
"Price falls must be attributed to bearish signals from related markets, first and foremost gas and German power," said Karsten Sander Nielsen, senior market analyst at Mind Energy.

Benchmark Dutch and British wholesale gas prices fell on hopes of a diplomatic solution to the US-Iran conflict that could help reinstate gas flows from the Middle East while most Norwegian maintenance is expected to conclude on Monday.
Germany's year-ahead power (TRDEBYc1), Europe's benchmark contract, fell €1.65, or 1.27%, to €128.25 per MWh.
In the European carbon market, the benchmark contract
fell €0.23, or about 0.26%, to €86.73 a ton.
"The week after next week will likely be more unsettled, wetter, and windier in continental Europe too," said LSEG meteorologist Georg Muller.
Nordic water reserves available 15 days ahead (PCAEC00) were seen at 15.41 terawatt hours (TWh) below normal, compared with 15.90 terawatt hours (TWh) below normal on Thursday.
